body: In case it wasn't clear, the failure is also intermittent in my continuous build - just built the same bits successfully.

Thanks for reporting.  It means that there's a bug in our snappy codec.  The offending test uses random data every time it runs and that's why it fails intermittently.  It's a kind of regression test and we need to add more failing test cases with non-random data.

Why not do something like this, then, so people can provide you with the data when it fails:
http://timboudreau.com/files/SnappyIntegrationTest.diff
Sounds like a great idea.  I think it will be even better to print a Java array definition.  Care to issue a pull request?

Yeah, but it occurred to me that the only thing that actually needs to be saved is the _seed_ of the Random - that should produce the same sequence of bytes on any VM.  The actual bytes are interesting when it comes to fixing it, but it would be a rather un-pretty with lots of longhand 16777216 element arrays...
You are right. Seed should be enough.

A pull request is a little more than I have time for right at the moment, but here's an updated version of SnappyIntegrationTest:  http://timboudreau.com/files/SnappyIntegrationTest.java

I included tests with a number of random seeds which fail - someone has some work to do :-)  Right now they're all set to appear to pass using @Test(expected=SomeThrowable.class) - I figure whoever needs to fix this probably will want to tackle these one-by-one since there are three flavors of exception here, so it's likely not just a single fix.
Thanks a lot! I've just integrated your changes into master.  @lw346, could you take a look?
Sure, I have this afternoon free.

There is a combination of 2 problems evidenced here:
- I'm a muppet, and decided that Short.MAX_VALUE should be 32768 instead of 32767.
- We need to check when generating our lookup table, that the nextIndex < maxIndex _\- 4_, as we attempt to read a 4 byte integer and hash it into our lookup table

As the fixes were so small, I've just pushed them straight to master: 7a8e9d7

I've also included an optimisation for encoding large outbound ByteBufs - the end of the data should be sent as an uncompressed chunk rather than as a compressed chunk, which will save us seeking through the data and building a hash table - this was done in 0bfa915.

@timboudreau Could you confirm that testRandom (and friends, now) are working across different systems?

Thanks @lw346.  I ran `testRandom()` with fairly large `RANDOM_RUNS` and it seems like we still get failures.  I pushed the updated `SnappyIntegrationTest` with failing tests.  Could you take a look again?

Another 2 problems:
- Not correctly parsing offset for 1-byte-offset copies
- Something to do with the use of buffers; if you modify the tests to use checksum validation, they all pass (with the above problem fixed) due to the SnappyFramedDecoder class creating a temporary output buffer

Should have both fixes pushed shortly.
